alt: The program reads a package weight and distance, computes a cost, and prints one of three labels. Three presets land exactly on the boundary between labels, showing which branch a tied cost takes.

steps.c: Python starts at the top of the file. Line 1 runs first.
Line 1 runs: `kg` is created with the value `10`.
Line 2 runs: `km` is created with the value `0`.
Line 4 runs: `cost` is created with the value `20`. `cost` is computed once, before any branch is checked, so every branch below reads the same value.
Line 6 checks the condition: it is true, so line 7 runs next. `cost <= 20` is `True` only for the first preset. A cost of `20` counts as `Standard`, not `Priority`.
Line 7 runs: it prints `Standard`. The program has finished: no lines are left to run.
